title: From Mount Nebo (Deuteronomy 34:1)
hookLine: Moses sees the whole land from the mountain
tomorrow: a kid asks about the rules. why does the answer start with a story?

lines: THE WHOLE TOWN IN ONE LOOK.
THE TORAH ENDS ON A HILLTOP.
cards: The top level of a parking garage, late on a summer night.

Noa and Owen climbed the stairs with two slushies, and Owen, laughing for the first time since his grandma's funeral, is pointing things out: the school, the water tower, her street, the park where they both learned to ride bikes.
The whole town fits in one look. She leaves for college in two weeks, and from up here it looks finished, like a model of itself. She goes quiet.
The Torah ends on a hilltop too. An old man climbs alone, and God shows him everything.

teach.h: UP FROM THE PLAINS OF MOAB.
teach.b: Deuteronomy's last chapter. Moses goes up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, across from Jericho, and God shows him all the land, north to south, out to the far sea.

teach.h: YOU SEE IT; YOU DON'T GO OVER.
teach.b: Then the hard line, in the JPS translation: "I have caused thee to see it with thine eyes, but thou shalt not go over thither."

He led a whole people through the wilderness toward this place, and he gets the view, not the walk. Some readers hear only grief in that. Others notice what the text adds a few verses on: "his eye was not dim."
He sees clearly, all the way to the end. Rashi, the medieval commentator, says God showed him more than hills and valleys; he showed him what would happen there, the good days and the hard ones.
Seeing it all means seeing the whole of something you won't finish. And here's a detail to tell someone tonight: the Torah says "no man knoweth of his sepulchre unto this day."

What's left of Moses is the teaching, and the people who walked on carrying it. A summit isn't the end of the road. It's the one place you can see the whole road, including the part that goes on without you.

how: Deuteronomy 34, Moses on Mount Nebo, is the Torah's last chapter; in synagogues it is read on Simchat Torah, when the yearly reading of the Torah ends and begins again at Genesis.

o: the whole land Moses was shown at the very end
the mountain where Moses was given the Torah
the hill where Moses was buried with honor

games.q: the last chapter of the Torah — tap the pairs.
p: where Moses saw the whole land
he sees it, but doesn't walk in
he saw clearly to the end
no one knows where it is

s: at the end of Deuteronomy, Moses walks into the land
he sees it from Nebo; the text says he will not go over.
the Torah says no one knows where Moses is buried
'no man knoweth of his sepulchre unto this day.'
by the end, Moses's eyesight had failed
the text says his eye was not dim.

games.q: your grandmother plants a row of fruit trees she says she'll never see full grown. a cousin calls it pointless. you've just heard about Nebo. what do you say?
o: seeing the whole of it counts, even if others walk in after.
the cousin's right; better not to start what you can't finish.
she should plant faster-growing ones so she gets to enjoy them.
games.why: Moses is shown the whole land and told he won't go over. the text doesn't call his work pointless: the people walk on with what he gave them.

practice: Go to the farthest view you can reach from where you are: a window, a doorway, a top step, a hallway with a long end. Let your eyes travel slowly from the nearest thing to the farthest, naming each one under your breath.
When you reach the edge of what you can see, stop naming, and just look.

wordCard.voice: From Mount Nebo: the view Moses was given at the end. The whole land, seen clearly, and walked by the people after him.

orig.note: Hebrew: Mount Nebo, in Moab, where Moses saw the land.

carryVoice: Your line: see it all. The view first, then the people walk on with what you gave them. Two of fourteen, and the air is thinner up here.
